title: Async & Messaging
summary: Decoupling the producer from the consumer. 10 building blocks drilled by recall: the signal that says reach for one, what it costs, how it breaks, which sibling rules it out, and what it is doing across the canonical problems.
keyTakeaways: Work Queue — A durable buffer of tasks between a producer and a pool of workers, so slow work happens outside the request path.
Pub/Sub — One published event delivered to every interested subscriber, so producers never learn who consumes them.
Fan-out — Turning one write into many per-recipient writes — precomputing on write (push) instead of assembling on read (pull).
Message Ordering — Guaranteeing that messages sharing a key are processed in the order they were produced — usually by binding a key to one partition.
At-Least-Once Delivery — The default durable-messaging guarantee: a message is redelivered until acknowledged, so it may arrive more than once but never zero times.
Exactly-Once (Effectively-Once) — Making duplicate delivery invisible in the result, by pairing at-least-once transport with idempotent or transactional application.
Dead-Letter Queue — A side channel for messages that have failed processing too many times, so one bad item cannot block the pipeline forever.

questions.prompt: Work Queue appears in 9 of the canonical design problems. Name as many as you can, and say what it is doing in each.
points: Design a Web Crawler — The URL frontier — the crawler's queue of what to fetch next, with politeness and priority encoded in how items are dequeued.
Design a Notification System — Decouples the triggering event from delivery, so a slow SMS provider cannot block push notifications or the request that caused them.
Design a Distributed Job Scheduler — The dispatch path: due jobs are enqueued and worker pools pull from it, which is what separates deciding-what-is-due from running-it.
Design an LLM Inference Platform — Inference requests wait for scarce GPU capacity rather than being rejected outright, with queue depth feeding the admission decision.
Design a Content Moderation Pipeline — Content awaiting automated scoring and human review moves through queues, decoupling upload throughput from review capacity.

Design a Financial Crime Alert Investigation System — Alerts arrive as an overnight batch and each investigation runs for minutes, so the queue is what decouples a 4K-alert dump from a fixed pool of concurrent investigations.
Design a Sanctions Screening System — Bulk re-screening after a list change is queued rather than run inline, because the two workloads share a matcher but not a latency budget.
Design a Human Review Queue — The workers are people, so the queue hands out leases rather than assignments and reclaims anything a reviewer abandons without needing the client to cooperate.

Design a Business Verification Pipeline — Verification hops have wildly different latencies, from a 2-second API call to a manual check taking days, so the work is queued per hop rather than held open per application.
